name: ROBOTIS OpenMANIPULATOR-X
description: A research- and education-grade 4-DOF desktop arm from ROBOTIS, the South Korean maker of DYNAMIXEL smart actuators, built around 5 all-metal-geared XM430-W350-T servos rather than hobby-grade hardware. Sold as a bare mechanical arm with no bundled controller, computer, or enclosure — it's designed to be paired with a separate U2D2 interface for PC/ROS control or an OpenCR board for standalone operation. An official ROS/ROS2 reference platform with deep MoveIt and Gazebo integration, genuinely Apache-2.0 licensed.

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: 711.37g total mass, per ROBOTIS's official e-Manual

specs.label: Software
specs.note: Apache-2.0 licensed; official MoveIt config and Gazebo simulation support

specs.label: Degrees of Freedom
specs.note: 4 arm joints + 1 gripper DOF — ROBOTIS's own phrasing, not a 6-axis arm

specs.label: Actuators
specs.note: full metal gear train, 12-bit magnetic absolute encoder, 0.25° rated backlash

specs.label: Controller
specs.note: needs a separate U2D2 (PC/ROS control) or OpenCR board (standalone Arduino control)

specs.label: Reach
specs.note: 500g rated payload; 4.1N·m stall torque per actuator limits payload at full extension

specs.label: Repeatability
specs.note: ROBOTIS-published spec — a real closed-loop figure, not a hobbyist estimate

specs.label: Construction
specs.note: exposed bus cabling between joints — no enclosure included

specs.label: Gripper
specs.note: 20–75mm stroke, prismatic mimic-joint design, same XM430 actuator class

specs.label: Maker
specs.note: South Korean, KOSDAQ-listed; designed as a TurtleBot3 companion manipulator

sourcing: Specs compiled from ROBOTIS's official e-Manual and product store listings, RobotShop and Generation Robots reseller listings, the ROBOTIS-GIT GitHub organization (LICENSE verified directly as Apache-2.0), the ROS ecosystem's own robot registry, and ROBOTIS/community forum threads, as of this build. Several details are flagged as unconfirmed above: an exact product release date, the precise meaning of the "X" in the name, and any specific university co-development partnership for the hardware itself — none were found in a citable primary source. This entry hasn't yet been cross-linked into the rest of the Robot Arms subcategory or synced to the directory listing; that's planned for a later pass.

pricing.summary: ROBOTIS's own US store and RobotShop both list the bare arm (SKU RM-X52-TNM) at **$1,629.09**, matched by Generation Robots in the EU at €1,739.56 incl. VAT. That price covers only the arm itself — a power supply, base plate, and controller interface are all sold separately, pushing a realistic working setup to roughly **$1,750–$1,900+**.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: OpenMANIPULATOR-X's software is genuinely Apache-2.0 licensed, with real ROS2 packages, a dedicated MoveIt config, and Gazebo simulation models — a substantive open-source integration, not a token wrapper. A 6-DOF configuration doesn't exist as a factory variant; it's only a user-contributed modification with a payload-capacity tradeoff flagged by ROBOTIS staff on their own forum.
